NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is a BMS firmware update that implements a Thermal‑Gradient Compensated Rest Balancing (TGCRB) algorithm: during every rest period (no charge/discharge for >1 h) the BMS wakes once per 24 h, measures all cell voltages, and applies the existing 1 A balancing current to the highest‑voltage cells (the cooler bottom cells) for a pre‑computed duration derived from the known 15 °C top‑to‑bottom gradient, holding the at‑rest cell‑to‑cell voltage spread below 35 mV.  
Standard practice balances only during charge using a fixed voltage threshold, never balances during rest, and does not compensate for the thermal gradient.  
Adjacent technique: “idle/storage balancing” exists in some BMS (e.g., periodic voltage‑threshold balancing while parked). Departure: TGCRB uses a position‑weighted, gradient‑derived schedule applied proactively, not reactively, so balancing charge exactly matches the predicted self‑discharge difference and no energy is wasted on unnecessary balancing.  
Mechanism: attacks the driving physics (temperature‑dependent self‑discharge differential) by proactively removing charge from the cooler cells at a rate that matches the predicted ΔI_sd, preventing the voltage spread from ever reaching the trip threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK
Driving variable = cell‑to‑cell voltage spread at rest (ΔV_rest).  
Governing relation: ΔV_rest ≈ (ΔI_sd · t) / (dQ/dV), where ΔI_sd is the self‑discharge current difference caused by the 15 °C gradient, t is rest time, and dQ/dV is the differential capacity. For NMC‑811 at 50 % SOC, dQ/dV ≈ 10 mV/%SOC, cell capacity ≈ 62 Ah. Typical self‑discharge at 25 °C ≈ 3 %/month (1.86 Ah/month); at 40 °C (top) ≈ 9 %/month (5.58 Ah/month). ΔI_sd ≈ (5.58‑1.86) Ah / 720 h ≈ 5.2 mA. Uncorrected daily ΔV_rest ≈ (5.2 mA × 24 h) / 62 Ah × (100 % / 10 mV) ≈ 2 mV/day → 35 mV in ~18 days.  
TGCRB applies balancing charge Q_bal = I_bal · t_bal to the higher‑voltage (cooler) cells. With I_bal = 1 A, daily correction requires t_bal = 0.12 Ah / 1 A = 7.2 min/day, well within the 1 A capability.  
DIRECTION‑OF‑EFFECT: driving variable = ΔV_rest; the mechanism moves it DOWN by applying balancing charge to the cooler cells; this REDUCES the failure driver.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| # | Item | Procurement tag | Notes |
|---|------|----------------|-------|
| 1 | BMS firmware update implementing TGCRB algorithm (wake schedule, voltage measurement, position‑weighted balancing duration calculation, hysteresis stop at 30 mV spread) | (c) | Parameter/procedure change on existing BMS microcontroller; delivered via standard OTA update mechanism. |
| 2 | Existing BMS hardware (microcontroller, cell‑voltage ADCs, balancing MOSFETs, 1 A balancing resistors) | (a) | Used as‑is; no hardware modification. |
| 3 | Existing 1 A balancing current capability | (a) | Used as‑is; duty cycle changed only. |
| 4 | One‑time commissioning procedure: measure/confirm top‑to‑bottom thermal gradient (or accept nameplate 15 °C) and store position‑weighting factors in BMS non‑volatile memory | (c) | Procedure change; uses existing temperature sensors (if present) or nameplate gradient; no new instrumentation. |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD‑PRACTICE PARITY)
| Aspect | Standard practice | TGCRB intervention | Burden comparison |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Hardware procurement | BMS + balancing circuits (catalog) | Identical (rows 2,3) | Same |
| Firmware development | Periodic OTA updates | One additional OTA update (row 1) | Same class (OTA update) |
| Commissioning | Basic voltage/temperature check | Adds gradient characterization step (row 4) | One extra procedure step; same labor class |
| Installation/commissioning | Standard cabinet install | Identical; firmware loaded during install | Same |
| Operation | Balance during charge only | Balance during charge + 7 min/day rest balancing | Energy loss = 1 A × 3.7 V × 0.12 h/day = 0.44 Wh/day (0.015 % of 3 kWh/day) → explicit near‑zero operational loss |
| Maintenance | None | None | Same |
| Cost class | Standard BMS + balancing | No new parts, no new tooling | Same or lower |

Conclusion: same‑or‑lower burden class in every row; operational loss explicitly priced at 0.44 Wh/day (negligible).

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol:  
1. Obtain two identical 13‑cell NMC‑811 modules (3 kWh each) with standard BMS.  
2. Load Module A with standard firmware (charge‑only balancing). Load Module B with TGCRB firmware.  
3. Place modules in an environmental chamber with a controlled 15 °C top‑to‑bottom gradient (heaters on top, coolers on bottom). Set both to 50 % SOC.  
4. No charge/discharge cycles for 6 months (accelerated at 35 °C average to compress calendar aging; gradient maintained at 15 °C).  
5. Record all cell voltages daily via the BMS (accuracy ±5 mV).  
Pass/fail thresholds:  
- PASS: Module B maximum cell‑to‑cell voltage spread at rest remains <35 mV for the entire test.  
- FAIL: Module B spread exceeds 35 mV at any measurement point.  
Kill criterion: If Module B exceeds 35 mV, the intervention is falsified.  
Duration: 6 months (or equivalent accelerated time).  
Instruments: Existing BMS voltage measurement (no added sensors); external thermocouples only for gradient verification (not part of deployed mechanism).
